newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO market volume, transactions to fall in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: OLO market volume, transactions to fall in 1997/98.

text.p: The number of transactions and volume on the secondary market in Belgian government bonds (OLOs) has been falling gradually this year and will continue to do so in the course of 1997 and 1998, Generale Bank said.

In its monthly report on the economy and markets, Mario Van Hemelryk of the bank's Belgian Franc Trading-Fixed Income department said that in 1996 daily trade on the secondary market for OLOs averaged 276 billion Belgian francs, up 10 percent on 1995.
But the average number of transactions per day fell to 571 in 1996 from 614 in 1995.
Van Hemelryk said it was as yet unclear how the market would look once OLOs were being issued in euro rather than Belgian francs from January 1, 1999 onwards.
Talks about this were being held between the National Bank, the Treasury and the primary dealers in OLOs, he said.
The primary dealer system, set up in 1991, requires selected dealers to make a market in OLOs by continuously quoting bid and ask prices.
They are allowed to take part in the Treasury's non-competitive OLO and Treasury bill auctions and enjoy a preferential relationship with the central bank.
